items.name: Creative non-fiction voice
items.intent: Essays that sound like a person rather than a content system: dry, concrete, unhurried. Not LinkedIn, not a manual. This is the hardest of the four, and it is here to show that even 'voice' partly mechanises.
items.carries: The hardest case: style and tone in creative non-fiction. About 40 % rule weight, judged remainder. It demonstrates that even 'voice' partly mechanises.

items.name: Technical explanation
items.intent: Correct, well-pitched technical prose for a named audience. Mixed on purpose: reading level and shape are rules, correctness and audience fit are judged, and the split is visible in the score method mix.
items.carries: Mixed: reading level, shape and self-repetition as rules; correctness and audience fit judged. The pack where the split is most visible in the score method mix.

items.name: House style compliance
items.intent: Copy that obeys a defined house style: our words, our register, our shape, our reading level. The point of this pack is that a style guide is mostly a list, and a list is a rule.
items.carries: Highest rule weight of the prose packs, about 70 %: banned terms, required disclosures, register, reading level and shape. The judged remainder is small.

items.name: Summary faithfulness
items.intent: Did the summary cover the source, and did it make anything up. This pack exists to show that 'did it hallucinate' is usually a deterministic question against an annotated source, not a matter of judgement.
items.carries: Mostly rung 3: claim coverage and unsupported-claim detection against annotated sources. It shows that 'did it make things up' is usually deterministic.
